newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka exports three pct of world's spice needs.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka exports three pct of world's spice needs.

text.p: Sri Lanka, which has been famous for its exotic spices since the 13th century, exported 13,500 tonnes last year, accounting for about three percent of the world's demand of 450,000 tonnes, a government minister said on Monday.
Cinnamon accounted for nearly 65 percent of the Indian Ocean island's exports, Trade Minister Kingsley Wickremaratne told a International Spice Group symposium without giving any comparative figures.
Other spices exported from Sri Lanka include clove, cardamom, pepper, nutmeg and mace, Wickremaratne said while opening a symposium for global spice growers and traders.
Some 40 overseas delegates from 20 countries will take part in the symposium in Colombo this week to work out means to boost spice exports, organisers said.

Jamaica's Hernal Hamilton, chairman of the international spice group, said spice can be intercropped with coconut or other plantations at little extra costs to generate significant additional income for the farmers.
